subject: Re: Rate replacement breakdown & migration timeline
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver@fluxdata.com>
To: camila.reyes@redwood.com
Cc: anya.liu@fluxdata.com, procurement@fluxdata.com
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Intro — pricing expectations and timeline for vendor swap

Camila —

Thanks for taking a look. We had a leadership call this morning and want to see a concrete replacement offer from Redwood that can match (or come close to) our current unit economics with our incumbent. Key asks from my side:

- A price floor for the first 12 months (per-token equivalent or committed vCPU/GPU hours)
- One-time onboarding credit or migration assistance (we have 6 models to port; two are high-risk due to KV cache size)
- A ramp timeline showing when performance parity will be expected per model class

Our incumbent is offering a 20% rebate for a 12-month committed spend plus two weeks of dedicated migration engineering. If Redwood can match or offset with credits + reduced list rate on the first 60 days, we can proceed to procurement immediately.

Attaching a short usage export for the last 3 months so you can model the costs (see attached).

—Oliver
Head of Platform, FluxData

Attachment: flux_usage_3mo.csv (referenced)

From: camila.reyes@redwood.com <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@fluxdata.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro — pricing expectations and timeline for vendor swap

Hi Oliver —

Appreciate the clarity and the export. I ran this by finance and product; we can put together an offer that narrows the delta. High level proposal (summary):

- Commercial: 15% list discount on token-based billing for months 1–12 plus a $60k onboarding credit applied as invoice credit over the first 3 invoices.
- Operational: 2 full weeks of dedicated migration support (engineering hours + 1 engagement manager) plus 30 days of elevated observability retention for immediate troubleshooting.
- Performance: we expect parity on most conversational workloads within 3–6 weeks of model onboarding; larger KV-cache models may require an extra 2–3 weeks of kernel tuning.

I attached a replacement economics workbook with modeled totals for your export and a tentative migration SOW. Can you confirm whether the onboarding credit needs to be applied to a specific legal entity or split across two subsidiaries?

If that looks reasonable I’ll loop in Vivek (discount approvals) and Ben (onboarding ops) and we’ll convert to a redlined DocuSign.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-replacement-offer-2026.pdf, sow-migration-draft.docx

From: ben.carter@redwood.com <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: camila.reyes@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Rate replacement breakdown & migration timeline

Camila —

Reviewed the workbook. A few implementation notes and constraints from Ops/Finance:

- The $60k onboarding credit is fine but should be structured as a non-recoupable service credit tied to the initial 12-month commit in the deal record. We should cap credits applied to usage vs. professional services split (suggest 70/30 usage/PS).
- For the two high KV-cache models, add an additional performance risk buffer: offer a 10% temporary credit for the first 30 days post-cutover if latency SLAs miss the agreed targets. That will reduce churn risk.
- We can commit 3 engineers (distributed across two weeks) and an engagement manager for onboarding; travel is not included.

Also recommend we leave room for a short-term pilot: 30-day pilot at a slightly elevated price that converts into the committed tier on signature. This lets FluxData validate the integration before full migration.

If you want to move forward I can draft the commercial terms to hand over to Legal for inclusion in the SOW.

—Ben Carter
Director, Sales Operations

Attachment referenced: flux_migration_estimate.xlsx

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: camila.reyes@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Rate replacement breakdown & migration timeline

Thanks team —

Quick governance note from pricing: Vivek, the combined concession schedule (15% list + $60k credit + 10% short-term SLA buffer) projects a 12-month net revenue delta of roughly -$85k on the modeled usage (see sheet: sensitivity tab). We need approval to proceed to a signed offer at that hit or propose alternate structuring: front-loaded credits or extended payment terms.

Vivek — do you want to approve as-is or request an alternate structure? If you approve, I’ll prepare the final terms and route to Legal for the DocuSign flow.

—Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Strategy

From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: camila.reyes@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, Oliver Grant <oliver@fluxdata.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Final — approved offer and next steps

Oliver / FluxData —

We ran the numbers and are prepared to move forward with the commercial package Camila outlined with these clarifications:

1) Commercial: 15% list discount months 1–12; $60,000 onboarding credit split 70/30 usage vs professional services and issued as invoice credits over the first three invoices.
2) SLA buffer: 10% temporary service credit for missed latency targets on the two high KV-cache models for the first 30 days post-cutover (automated credit, no claims needed).
3) Pilot: 30-day pilot at standard list rate with a guaranteed conversion to the committed discount if pilot metrics are met.

Ops commitments: Redwood will assign 3 engineers and an engagement manager. Expected cutover timeline: pilot kickoff within 2 weeks of signature; full migration completed within 8 weeks of pilot success (timeline contingent on FluxData providing model artifacts and test harness within 5 business days of kickoff).

Camila — please send the final redlined terms and DocuSign link. Oliver — confirm if FluxData wants the onboarding credit invoiced to the US parent or split across two legal entities; if split, provide the allocation percentages.

Looking forward to getting you onboarded.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-replacement-offer-2026.pdf, flux_migration_estimate.xlsx
